subject: physics
question_text: Prove that the average kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Short Answer Question 4 (printed p.139). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: from the kinetic-theory pressure formula P = ⅓(N/V)mv̄², PV = ⅓Nmv̄² = ⅔N(½mv̄²); equating with the gas equation PV = Nk_BT gives ½mv̄² = (3/2)k_BT, so the average kinetic energy of a molecule is directly proportional to the absolute temperature.

steps.margin_note: This starting formula must be written and multiplied by V.
steps.why: Starting from the kinetic-theory pressure formula, rather than assuming the final result, is what makes this a proof and not a restatement.
common_mistakes: Starting directly from ½mv̄² = (3/2)k_BT. That is the result to be proved, so it cannot be the starting point of a proof.
steps.memory_tip: Start from P = ⅓(N/V)mv̄², the derived kinetic-theory formula, not the final result.

steps.label: Rewrite as energy

steps.margin_note: The rewritten form PV = ⅔N(½mv̄²) must appear.
steps.why: Splitting the ⅓ into ⅔ times ½ turns the formula into N times the average kinetic energy of one molecule, ½mv̄², which is the quantity the proof is about.
common_mistakes: Leaving the formula as ⅓Nmv̄² and comparing it directly with Nk_BT — the ½mv̄² term must appear before the comparison.
steps.memory_tip: ⅓ splits into ⅔ times ½ — that ½ is the average kinetic energy per molecule.

steps.why: This is the second, independent expression for the same PV, and the proof works by setting the two equal.
common_mistakes: Writing PV = nRT and not connecting n and R to N and k_B (nR = Nk_B).
steps.memory_tip: PV = Nk_BT is the gas equation written per molecule, not per mole.

steps.margin_note: The final boxed line ½mv̄² = (3/2)k_BT is where this mark is earned.
steps.why: Cancelling N and isolating ½mv̄² leaves an expression with only T and constants on the other side, which is exactly the definition of direct proportionality.
common_mistakes: Stopping at ⅔N(½mv̄²) = Nk_BT without cancelling N and isolating ½mv̄² — the proportionality is not shown until this last line.
steps.memory_tip: Cancel the N, and only T and constants remain — that IS the proportionality.

insider_note: This is a prove question — every algebra step from P = ⅓(N/V)mv̄² to the final line must be shown; stating ½mv̄² = (3/2)k_BT alone earns none of these marks.
